findings.text: the wait pass calls the per-tick hook every poll, and the hook now writes the checkpoint unconditionally, so a follower whose producer is live and whose stream says nothing rewrites its checkpoint (temp sibling, file fsync, os.replace, directory fsync: reckon/crew/follow_checkpoint.py:223-239) at the poll rate with an unchanged offset — measured as 24 inode changes in 3 s of an idle live-producer arming delivering exactly 2 rows, against 0 in the no-producer control (idle-checkpoint-writes.log); gate the write on the offset or identity differing from what was last written.

the section's archived record still reads '6 passed' for tests/test_follow_rearm_continues.py and lists three mutations, while the reviewed head carries 15 tests and a fourth mutation; the plan page's own record at docs/plans/the-fleet-counters-count-the-fleet.html:182 likewise says 5 tests and never names the pane history, and both files were last touched by 8183a9fd — so the section's persistent record understates the reviewed head and a later reader cannot see that the history requirement landed.

cap_history's trim returns fresh[-max_rows:], which for a max_rows of 0 returns every row rather than none, because Python's fresh[-0:] is fresh[0:]; the config floor history_rows >= 1 makes it unreachable through flight config today, but the function is the module's own public trimming contract and zero is exactly what a caller reaching for 'no history' would pass.
